name: Spironolactone
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Heart failure (NYHA III-IV, reduced EF), K ≤5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >50
usual_adult_dose.dose: 25 mg once daily; may increase to 50 mg once daily
25 to 100 mg daily in single or divided doses
100 mg daily; start in hospital for cirrhosis and titrate slowly

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Potassium supplements and potassium-raising drugs (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs, heparin/LMWH, trimethoprim)
key_interactions.action: Usually stop potassium supplements in heart failure; check potassium when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy changes.

key_interactions.effect: Weaker diuretic and antihypertensive effect (and potassium rise).

key_interactions.action: Monitor; the label reports the effect.

common: Gynecomastia (most common; about 9% of men in RALES at a mean 26 mg/day)
serious: Hypotension and worsening kidney function from excessive diuresis
Electrolyte and metabolic abnormalities (hyponatremia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia, hypochloremic alkalosis, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia)

monitoring: Serum potassium within 1 week of starting or titrating, then regularly (more often with other potassium-raising drugs)
Electrolytes, uric acid and blood glucose periodically

pk.half_life: Spironolactone 1.4 hours; canrenone 16.5 hours; TMS 13.8 hours; HTMS 15 hours
pk.half_life_eskd: Not studied: renal impairment PK not specifically studied (label)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Metabolites mainly in urine, secondarily in bile
